summary: Steel fire tower on Boyers Knob south of Shamokin, PA: built 1921, removed 1975 per FFLOS. Papers give 67 ft (plan) and 47 ft; a 2014 DEP reclamation project covers the site.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower (FFLOS register); steel structure (1927 newspaper)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1975, according to the FFLOS register.

staffing.status: Towerman on duty in the fire season in the 1920s; tower reopened in August 1930 after a serious fire situation

facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forests and Waters (1927 newspaper)

events.note: Register gives 1921; an October 1921 newspaper says erection had begun, for a planned 67-foot tower
John Deitrich placed in charge, November 1922; earliest staffing found
M.C. Beck had been towerman for three years and was expected back in spring 1927
Tower reopened in August 1930 after a serious fire situation; John A. Scott, Jr. called back to take charge
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg
State reclamation project at the site (December 31, 2012 to April 18, 2014) removed three hazardous structures; the fact sheet does not name the lookout tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A October 1921 newspaper gave a planned 67-foot tower; a 1927 newspaper describes a 47-foot steel structure. The record uses 47 feet (14.3 m), the later description of the built tower. The 67-foot figure may have been the plan and was not confirmed as built.

sources.title: Boyers Knob Lookout Abandoned Mine Reclamation Project, Fact Sheet

notes_for_editor: Height: 67 ft in the 1921 notice vs 47 ft in the 1927 article; the register gives no height, and the 14.3 m in the brief matches 47 ft. The 1975 removal date rests on the register alone. The DEP fact sheet is for the reclamation project named after the lookout; it does not say the tower was removed by that project, and its 'currently' means 2014. Access and visit facts were not established, so they are omitted. Newspaper text is as reproduced on the Eastern page; the originals were not checked.
